metadata.title: SPARC EC2 Secrets Manager (Application) Component Definition

components.title: AWS Secrets Manager (SPARC Application Secrets)
components.description: Secrets Manager secret containing all SPARC application configuration including auto-generated SECRET_KEY_BASE, authentication settings (OIDC, LDAP), SMTP credentials, and operational parameters. Deployed via Terraform (AWS/EC2/modules/secrets/). <!-- UPDATE: Insert secret ARN and name for your deployment. -->

control-implementations.description: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control implementations for application secrets management

implemented-requirements.description: Authenticator Management: SECRET_KEY_BASE is auto-generated as a 128-character random string via Terraform random_password — it is never manually set or stored in configuration files. OIDC client secrets, LDAP bind passwords, and SMTP passwords are stored in Secrets Manager rather than in environment variables, tfvars files, or source code. All secrets are encrypted at rest with AWS KMS. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000175.

Protection of Information at Rest: All application secrets are encrypted at rest using AWS KMS within Secrets Manager. This includes SECRET_KEY_BASE, OIDC client secrets, LDAP bind password, and SMTP password. Secrets are never written to disk in plaintext — they are injected into the EC2 instance at runtime via the Secrets Manager integration. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000231.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Secrets Manager uses AES-256 encryption via KMS. Consider using a customer-managed KMS key for additional control over encryption key lifecycle.

implemented-requirements.description: Access Enforcement: Access to application secrets is restricted to the EC2 instance role via a resource-level IAM policy granting only secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the specific secret ARN. No other IAM principals have access. The secret is not accessible from the console without explicit IAM permissions. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000033.
implemented-requirements.remarks: IAM policy in the iam module restricts access to both db_secret_arn and app_secret_arn specifically.

implemented-requirements.description: Identification and Authentication: The secrets module manages authentication configuration for multiple identity providers: local login (username/password with configurable password expiry), OIDC/OAuth2 (Okta, Entra ID, Keycloak, Auth0), and LDAP. MFA can be enforced via OIDC provider (SPARC_OIDC_FORCE_MFA). Session timeout is configurable (SPARC_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES). Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000148.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Authentication method selection is controlled by SPARC_ENABLE_LOCAL_LOGIN, SPARC_ENABLE_OIDC, and SPARC_ENABLE_LDAP flags.

implemented-requirements.description: Account Management: Application-level account management is configured via secrets: user self-registration (SPARC_ENABLE_USER_REGISTRATION), auto-deactivation after inactivity (SPARC_INACTIVITY_DAYS), and password expiry (SPARC_PASSWORD_EXPIRY_DAYS). These settings enforce organizational account lifecycle policies within the SPARC application. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000023.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Default: registration disabled, 30-day inactivity timeout, 30-day password expiry. Configurable via Terraform variables.

implemented-requirements.description: Event Logging: Secrets Manager logs all secret access events (GetSecretValue) to AWS CloudTrail, providing an audit trail of when secrets were retrieved and by which IAM principal. Application logging configuration (SPARC_LOG_LEVEL, SPARC_STRUCTURED_LOGGING) is managed here, enabling structured JSON output for CloudWatch/SIEM integration. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000089.
implemented-requirements.remarks: CloudTrail records all Secrets Manager API calls. SPARC_STRUCTURED_LOGGING=true enables JSON log format for automated log analysis.
